title: Almost every finite Markov kernel coalesces under every grand coupling
description:
This note answers Grimmett and Holmes's Open Problem 3.8 in Coalescence in Markov Chains (Journal of Theoretical Probability, 2026). For any fixed number of states, row normalization of an independent Uniform(0,1) array gives almost surely a kernel for which every consistent grand coupling coalesces. The claim concerns successive independent and identically distributed maps sharing the given one-state marginals. It also holds for any absolutely continuous law on the row-stochastic kernels.

Take an idempotent of minimum rank in the semigroup generated by the coupling support. After compression by that idempotent, every supported map permutes one representative per fiber. Averaging those permutations gives a doubly stochastic compression of the fixed kernel. A rank k at least two forces k−1 independent affine equations. Finitely many idempotents therefore give one null exceptional family for all coupling laws. This uses classical minimum-rank semigroup structure, credited to Högnäs, and goes beyond the earlier block-coupling and positive-measure conclusions.

For any fixed kernel outside the displayed subspaces, discard maps below an explicit mass threshold. A noncoalescing retained support would contradict the kernel's minimum deviation from the affine equations. A bounded-length synchronizing word among retained maps gives an exponential tail uniform over grand couplings of that kernel. The certificate is sufficient and does not give a classification on the exceptional subspaces.

The standard-library replay checks all 233 nonsynchronizing supports of up to three maps on three states and 389 minimum-rank idempotent compressions. It checks 17 mixtures for the worked example, which has a coupling whose initial coalescing pair is random. Adding positive constant-map weight makes the example avoid all seven rank-at-least-two obstruction subspaces. The release includes the paper and source, a rotating figure, the offline explorer and checksum-ledgered evidence. External peer review and formal verification are pending.

ChatGPT Astra 6.2 (OpenAI) generated the recovered proof and original replay under human direction. OpenAI Codex independently reviewed the mathematics. GPT-6.2 Sol (OpenAI) checked primary sources and prepared the manuscript, extended replay and illustration. DannyExperiments is the project citation identity.
